synthesis.content:
### Central insight
Use the two names to clarify where each type of flow occurs and what distinguishes them.

### Evidence
NOAA describes rip currents as powerful narrow channels of fast-moving water, present along U.S. ocean coasts and Great Lakes shores, moving at up to eight feet per second. A rip tide describes swift tidal water through inlets and certain mouths.

### Gaps and uncertainty
Treat the speed as an upper bound, not a usual speed. Center the distinction in names and locations.
